column2: Too tired. I'd nap till dinner.
I went back to my room and collapsed onto the bed fully dressed.
I had barely started to doze when a knock echoed through the room.
I hardly felt like I'd slept, but there was nothing to be done.
I headed to the dining room.
Knives and forks were already set on the dining room tables.
The three girls and the couple who had just arrived were already seated.
I sat down at the table where {n2} had quickly taken a seat.
In the middle of the table stood a candle shaped like a Christmas tree.
Its small flickering flame faintly lit {n2}'s profile as she gazed out the window.
let me take my time choosing.”
I couldn't make up my mind.
“That thin one with the long hair, of course!”
{n2} had stomped hard on my foot.
{n2}'s elbow had landed right in my solar plexus.
“That one with the glasses is nice, too.”
{n2}'s nails were twisting the back of my hand.
I was just answering the question…”
The pain brought tears to my eyes.
“You're not thinking dirty thoughts, are you?”
“Of course not, that's not what I meant.”
“You're not thinking dirty thoughts, are you?”
“Of course not, that's not what I meant.”
{n2} said that, but she sounded more amused than disdainful, which was a relief.
But the man didn't answer and just kept silently spooning soup into his mouth.
If he doesn't answer, he's probably not a yakuza.
Maybe he keeps his sunglasses on because they're a keepsake from his parents, or because they have a built-in radio and he's listening to rokyoku {C3}(sung storytelling){C0}.
Either way, once our food was brought out, none of that mattered at all anymore.
{n2} groaned after one sip of soup.
Crumbling grains of rice floated in a gray liquid that looked like dissolved lime.
I had never seen or heard of such a strange dish.
That lukewarm soup was truly awful, and it made me feel sick to the core.
The dishes that followed were all unsatisfying in both taste and portion, and sighs could be heard from all around.
As an inn, maybe, but as a restaurant, this place could never make it…
Just as I was starting to think that, Mr. Kobayashi rushed into the dining room in a panic.
“Everyone, I'm terribly sorry!{r}{p}That dish was a mistake.{r}{p}We'll bring you the proper one right away, so please don't touch it!”
The Kobayashis and the part-timers scrambled to clear the tables, and five minutes later new dishes were laid out.
“Thank you for waiting.{r}{p}This is the true Spur menu.{r}{p}Please, enjoy your meal at your leisure.{r}{p}We sincerely apologize for the mistake.”
Mr. Kobayashi apologized with a look of near-tears and fled back to the kitchen.
We timidly brought the new dishes to our mouths.
{n2} exclaimed after one sip of soup.
The taste more than made up for the earlier disappointment.
“But what on earth was that earlier?”
{n2} smiled mischievously and glanced toward Midori, who was cleaning up a little way off.
She always makes that face when she does.
When I asked, Midori suddenly looked troubled.
“That's, um, not something I can say...{p}It's fine, it's definitely not bad for you...{r}{p}I'm sorry, I have to clean up quickly or I'll...”
She scurried off to another table.
that was Aunt's doing.{r}{p}...Honestly, what are we going to do with her.”
“But Aunt wants to show off her skills too, and sometimes she serves the guests her own cooking behind Uncle's back...”
“That costs them about twenty percent of their customers.”
“Aunt would be a wonderful wife if only she didn't do that.{r}{p}But Uncle's cooking was good, wasn't it?”
Remembering it made my mouth water again.
“Uncle loves cooking.{r}{p}He says he wanted to be a chef since he was a kid.”
“He gave it up once and became a yamabushi, but he never got any good at the conch horn.{r}{p}Since they couldn't have children either, he returned to secular life and started an inn.”
“From yamabushi to inn, that's quite a leap...”
But my grandfather, that is, my mother's father...”
“That grandfather was a yamabushi {C3}(mountain ascetic){C0} himself from the start.”
“Oh, so it was almost like taking over the family business.”
Plus, that grandfather owned several mountains around here.{r}{p}So since they had the land from the start, they don't seem to have struggled on that front.”
I felt a bit of kinship with him somehow.
“Flaky, you say, but my uncle once won the All-Japan Best Yamabushi Grand Prize.”
it's a prestigious prize that's been given for over two hundred years.{r}{p}He's not good with the conch horn, but he won it through effort.”
“My apologies, I'm impressed.{r}{p}Then quitting must have been hard, huh.”
since you're an acquaintance of the owner,
I think he won't charge you...”
{n2} suddenly stood up and left the dining room.
I followed her out of the dining room.
“But it's better to settle these things properly...”
“It's down to how the boss trains his people.
An ominous air hung in the room.
“Well then, I'll go prepare three more servings.”
With that, she took the tray and headed to the kitchen.
Somehow, the mood returned to normal.
“Someone will die tonight… a threat letter said.”
someone is going to die tonight…”{g}
Oops, said like that it's way too blunt…{g}
But either they didn't hear me or nobody reacted to what I said.{g}
I seem to have dropped my voice too low trying to sound menacing.{g}
First, saw through the neck: rrr-rrr, rrr-rrr.
Then snip the crunchy heel tendons with a box cutter.
Damn, my hands are getting slippery with blood!
Wiping them with a towel… five minutes.
No wait, wait, a towel's fine if there is one, but…
“Even estimating as short as possible, I think it would take thirty minutes.”
Mr. Kobayashi, unable to wait for my answer, carried the conversation on.
Well, if you were efficient, maybe that's about right.
Could the motive have been a grudge so deep that merely killing wouldn't settle it?
Even so, can a person really do something like that for that reason alone?
I decided to check whether the bath towel was damp.
The bath towel was dry and showed no sign of having been used.
“I know who's behind all the incidents.”
So you know who killed Mr. Tanaka too?”
“So you only know who killed Midori?”
The only person who could possibly be the culprit…
Everyone stared at me blankly for a while.
Are you saying you killed Mr. Tanaka and Shinozaki?”
Mr. Kobayashi cried out in confusion.
That can't be right, can it?{p}
I was with {n1} almost the whole time…”
I killed them both with these hands.”
I stared at my hands and giggled.
Mr. Kobayashi asked, still looking unable to believe it.
There's no reason.{r}{p}I killed them because I wanted to kill them.{r}{p}It felt great.”
Toshio leaped at me as I kept laughing.
In his hand he gripped a gleaming kitchen knife.
wait a minute…{p}That was just a joke…”
The knife slid into my belly with surprising ease.
I sank to my knees and fell forward.
“Me?{r}{p}…Is that supposed to be a joke?{r}{p}
